newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan firms say buy stake in Occidental oil rights.
newsitem.headline: Japan firms say buy stake in Occidental oil rights.

text.p: Japan's Marubeni Corp and Japan Petroleum Exploration Co Ltd (JAPEX) said on Thursday they had bought a 30 percent stake in exploration rights held by U.S. Occidental Petroleum Corp in Pakistan, Peru and Ireland.
Marubeni and JAPEX said they had formed a new firm called Global Petroleum Co Ltd as of February 14, 1997, to carry out the venture.
The agreement was heralded by the two companies as a contribution to the stable supply of oil to Japan.

The farm out deal will allow the new company to undertake oil and gas exploration activities in four separate blocks, with a 30 percent undivided interest of what Occidental holds in each area, the Japanese firms said in a statement.
Global Petroleum Co plans to invest four to five billion yen ($43.4 million) in the project over the next two years.
The Occidental acreage lies in Ireland's offshore Porcupine basin, Pakistan's Salt Range concession, and Block 72 in the West of Peru's Maranon basin, the companies said.
Probable oil and gas reserves in the regions were described as considerable, but were not detailed.
The new company will be based in Tokyo and will be headed by Tadami Katahira, the executive vice president of JAPEX.
Masaaki Hayakawa, director of Marubeni Corp, will serve as the new company's executive vice president, the companies said.
